lesson.title: Place Value to 999: Compare, Order and Round Numbers
lesson.explanation: A three-digit number has hundreds, tens and ones. The position of a digit determines its value: in 432, the 4 represents 400, the 3 represents 30, and the 2 represents 2. To compare numbers, compare hundreds first; if they are equal, compare tens, then ones. To round to the nearest ten, look at the ones digit. To round to the nearest hundred, look at the tens digit: 5 or more rounds up, while 0–4 rounds down.

practice_problems.question: What is the value of the 4 in 432?
hints: Read the position of the digit.
practice_problems.explanation: The 4 is in the hundreds place, so it means four hundreds.

practice_problems.question: Round 467 to the nearest ten.
practice_problems.explanation: The ones digit is 7, so round up to the next ten.

practice_problems.question: Round 834 to the nearest hundred.
hints: Look at the tens digit when rounding to hundreds.
practice_problems.explanation: The tens digit is 3, so round down to 800.

practice_problems.question: Which is greater: 589 or 598?
practice_problems.explanation: Both have 5 hundreds; 9 tens is more than 8 tens.

practice_problems.question: Write 706 in expanded form.
hints: Write the value contributed by each place.

practice_problems.question: Arrange 305, 350 and 503 from smallest to largest.
practice_problems.explanation: 305 and 350 have 3 hundreds; compare tens. 503 has 5 hundreds and is largest.

practice_problems.question: A learner rounds 264 to 200 when rounding to the nearest hundred. Is this correct? Explain.
practice_problems.answer: No. The tens digit is 6, so 264 rounds up to 300.
hints: Look at the tens digit, not the ones digit.
practice_problems.explanation: When rounding to hundreds, tens 5–9 rounds to the next hundred.

hints: Use hundreds, tens and ones; the position changes the digit's value.
To round to tens, inspect ones; to round to hundreds, inspect tens.
When comparing, start at the leftmost digit and move right only when digits are equal.

key_vocabulary.definition: One of the symbols 0 through 9 used to write numbers.
The amount a digit represents because of its position.
Writing a number as the sum of its place values.
Replacing a number with a nearby ten or hundred to make it easier to use.
key_vocabulary.example_usage: 467 rounds to 470 to the nearest ten.

misconceptions.misconception: The digit itself is always its value.
misconceptions.correction: Its value depends on place; 4 means 400 in the hundreds place, but 40 in the tens place.
misconceptions.why_students_think_this: The digit and its place value are related but not identical.

misconceptions.misconception: When rounding, always look at the ones digit.
misconceptions.correction: Use the digit immediately to the right of the place you are rounding to.
misconceptions.why_students_think_this: The relevant digit changes when rounding to tens or hundreds.

items.question: What is the value of the 7 in 572?
items.hint: The 7 is in the tens place.

items.hint: Identify the hundreds, tens and ones.

items.question: Explain how to compare 419 and 391.
items.correct_answer: 419 is greater because it has 4 hundreds while 391 has 3 hundreds.

items.question: A learner rounds 751 to 700 to the nearest hundred. Is it correct?
items.correct_answer: No. The tens digit is 5, so 751 rounds up to 800.
items.hint: For nearest hundred, look at the tens digit.

items.question: Create a three-digit number that rounds to 500 to the nearest hundred and explain why.
items.correct_answer: Answers vary; any number from 450 through 549 rounds to 500 under the usual school rounding rule.
items.hint: Choose a number at least 450 and below 550.
